key_insight: Off-policy instability in asynchronous RL is not governed by ratio magnitude alone; it depends on token entropy, which changes how stale data should be trusted.
engineering_relevance: Entropy-aware filtering can stabilize large-scale LLM post-training in asynchronous pipelines, improving throughput without sacrificing accuracy.
method: Scale each token’s importance-ratio deviation by its local entropy.
Apply an entropy-scaled trust region instead of a uniform ratio threshold.
Avoid extra forward passes and version-switch detection.
evidence_signal: The method outperforms prior asynchronous approaches on long-horizon agentic and mathematical reasoning benchmarks, and matches synchronous GRPO accuracy while training 2.6× faster.
watch_item: Performance may depend on reliable token-level entropy estimates, so implementation details and hyperparameter tuning could affect stability.
paper_title: Deconstructing Off-Policy Ratios: Entropy-Scaled Trust Regions for Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning
